channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Tajik specialists study advanced cotton cultivation technologies in China
item.description: Tajik specialists have studied Chinese cotton cultivation and breeding technologies during a visit to China. The delegation included representatives from the Food Security Committee, the Tajik Academy of Agricultural Sciences, and private enterprises. They explored high-yield, drought-resistant cotton varieties and digital monitoring systems.

item.title: Astana and Phnom Penh to become sister cities; Kazakhstan and Cambodia sign agreements
item.description: Astana and Phnom Penh will become sister cities following the signing of six memorandums of cooperation between Kazakhstan and Cambodia. The agreements cover digital government, trade, culture, and tourism, signed in the presence of the leaders of both nations.

item.title: Kazakh President and Cambodian Prime Minister issue joint statement after talks
item.description: Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev and Cambodian Prime Minister Hun Manet issued a joint statement following expanded talks. During the meeting, both sides exchanged intergovernmental and interdepartmental documents, including memorandums on digital government, trade, culture, and tourism cooperation.

item.title: Kazakh President Tokayev Invites Cambodian Prime Minister to Explore Alem.ai Developments
item.description: Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev invited Cambodian Prime Minister Hun Manet and his delegation to explore Kazakhstan's artificial intelligence advancements at the international center Alem.ai. Tokayev highlighted the significant potential for high-tech cooperation, noting Cambodia's interest in AI development. The visit aims to showcase AI achievements and foster broader collaboration between the two nations.

item.title: Hidden Warehouses with Illegally Stored Medicines Worth 5.2 Billion Som Found in Namangan
item.description: Authorities in Namangan have uncovered hidden warehouses containing illegally stored medicines valued at approximately 5.2 billion Uzbek som. Three individuals were found to have organized five secret storage facilities in residential homes, stockpiling foreign-produced pharmaceuticals smuggled into Uzbekistan for resale. A total of 46,865 units of 287 different types of medicines were seized.

item.title: Kazakh President Tokayev and Cambodian Prime Minister Hun Manet Hold Expanded Talks
item.description: Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev and Cambodian Prime Minister Hun Manet held expanded talks, marking a new chapter in bilateral relations. Tokayev emphasized the 32-year history of constructive dialogue and cooperation, noting Kazakhstan views Cambodia as a reliable partner in Southeast Asia and a key link to ASEAN countries.

item.title: Cambodian Prime Minister Notes Graduates of Kazakh Universities Now Hold Governorships
item.description: Cambodian Prime Minister Hun Manet stated that many Cambodians who studied in Kazakhstan now hold high government positions, including provincial governorships and roles in ministries. He made these remarks during talks with President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev, highlighting the strong human connections and shared history between the two nations. The visit marks 32 years of diplomatic relations.

item.title: Kazakhstan and Cambodia Adopt Joint Statement Following Astana Talks
item.description: Kazakhstan and Cambodia have adopted a joint statement aimed at further developing bilateral cooperation, following talks between President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev and Prime Minister Hun Manet in Astana. The statement officially enshrines a shared vision for the future. Kazakhstan views Cambodia as a reliable partner in Southeast Asia and a key link to ASEAN countries.

item.title: Kazakh President and Cambodian Prime Minister Hold Expanded Talks in Astana
item.description: Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev and Cambodian Prime Minister Hun Manet held expanded talks in Astana, emphasizing that the latter's first visit to Kazakhstan opens the way for revitalizing bilateral relations. President Tokayev noted that Kazakhstan views Cambodia as a reliable partner in Southeast Asia and an important link for expanding cooperation with ASEAN countries.

item.title: Kazakhstan and Netherlands to Expand Agricultural Cooperation
item.description: The fourth meeting of the Kazakh-Dutch working group on agriculture took place in The Hague. Discussions focused on cooperation in seed production, agricultural science, animal health, aquaculture, and phytosanitary security. Both sides signed a joint statement on further agricultural cooperation, and partnerships were established between Wageningen University and Kazakh Agro-Technical Research University.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Court Declares Opposition Movement 'Shumkar' Extremist
item.description: The Oktyabrsky District Court in Bishkek has declared the informational materials and activities of the opposition media project 'Shumkar' extremist. This ruling affects individuals associated with the movement, including political blogger Syrgak Kenzhebaev and former Kumtor external manager Tengiz Bolturuk. The court's decision, published by the Prosecutor General's office, targets the group's activities, not necessarily its individual members.

item.title: Kazakhstan Government Plans Major Social Payment Cuts to Save Trillions of Tenge
item.description: The Kazakh government is preparing to significantly reduce social payments to affluent citizens, aiming to save 2.5 trillion tenge over three years. Prime Minister Olzhas Bektenov stated this aims to eliminate inequities where wealthy and low-income families receive similar support. Approximately 1.38 million households with incomes over 305,000 tenge per person monthly will be affected.

item.title: Kazakhstan Joins Budapest Convention on Cybercrime, Enhancing International Cooperation
item.description: Kazakhstan has officially joined the Council of Europe's Convention on Cybercrime, also known as the Budapest Convention. The Ministry of Foreign Affairs stated this provides a legal framework for cooperation with member states to combat computer crimes, improve operational interaction, and enhance law enforcement effectiveness in the digital sphere.

item.title: UN Women Reports 426 Million Women and Girls to Live in Extreme Poverty by 2026
item.description: UN Women estimates that 426 million women and girls globally will face extreme poverty in 2026. On the International Day for the Eradication of Poverty, the agency urged increased investment in social protection, healthcare, and education. UN Women stressed the need for governments to ensure equal opportunities and improve economic and social conditions for women and girls.

item.title: CIS Countries to Develop Common Approaches to Medical Services and Blood Donation Quality Control
item.description: The CIS Interparliamentary Assembly's commission on social policy and human rights met in St. Petersburg to discuss blood donation and infant food marketing regulation. Participants approved a draft model law on blood and component donation, outlining principles, safety requirements, and donor rights. Recommendations on regulating children's food marketing were also adopted.

item.title: Prominent Aktobe Doctor Receives Suspended Sentence for Embezzling 53 Million Tenge
item.description: A former chief physician in Aktobe, Zhanvek Narmukhamedov, received a five-year suspended sentence for embezzling 53 million tenge from the Social Health Insurance Fund. He allegedly created false patient records for services not rendered through his clinic, 'Medina Clinic,' and used the funds for personal needs. Narmukhamedov pleaded guilty and compensated the damages.

item.title: Cambodia Interested in Kazakhstan's E-Government Experience
item.description: Cambodia's ministries are keen to adopt Kazakhstan's experience in digital public services. Prime Minister Hun Manet expressed this interest during a meeting with President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev in Astana. He highlighted Kazakhstan's significant experience and advanced developments in e-government, proposing an exchange of expertise.

item.title: Kazakhstan's foreign trade turnover reached $103 billion in January-August
item.description: Kazakhstan's foreign trade turnover reached $103 billion in January-August, a 12.8% increase compared to the same period last year. Exports grew by 19.5% and imports by 4.5%, according to the Ministry of Trade and Integration. Sunflower oil exports rose 48.5% to $672.8 million, and grain exports increased by 26.5%.

item.title: Kazakhstan President and Cambodian Prime Minister Hold One-on-One Talks
item.description: Kazakhstan's President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev and Cambodian Prime Minister Hun Manet held one-on-one talks in Akorda. Tokayev noted the visit's historical significance and potential to boost bilateral relations and cooperation. Discussions covered trade, economic ties, and opening direct flights.

item.title: Kazakh President Welcomes Cambodian Prime Minister at Akorda
item.description: Kazakhstan's President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev welcomed the Prime Minister of Cambodia at Akorda. The meeting emphasized the historical significance of the visit and the potential for developing mutually beneficial cooperation between the two countries. Discussions included strengthening trade and economic ties.

item.title: Interior Ministry Denies Police Involvement in Korday Rape Allegation
item.description: Kazakhstan's Interior Ministry has denied allegations that police officers were involved in the alleged gang rape of a foreign national in Korday. The ministry stated that two suspects have been detained and the investigation is nearing completion. They urged the public to rely only on official sources for information regarding the case.

item.title: Cambodia Expresses Interest in Exchanging Experiences with Kazakhstan
item.description: Cambodian Prime Minister Hun Manet held talks with Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev, expressing Cambodia's interest in exchanging experiences with Kazakhstan. Tokayev highlighted the historical significance of the visit and the potential for developing mutually beneficial cooperation, including direct flights and humanitarian exchanges.

item.title: Tokayev Proposes Direct Flights Between Kazakhstan and Cambodia
item.description: During talks with Cambodian Prime Minister Hun Manet, Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev proposed exploring the possibility of opening direct flights between the two countries. Tokayev also emphasized strengthening trade-economic ties and expanding humanitarian exchanges, noting the potential for cooperation in the energy sector.

item.title: Tanker Carrying 2 Million Barrels of Oil Explodes in Strait of Hormuz
item.description: A tanker carrying over 2 million barrels of oil exploded in the Strait of Hormuz after hitting a mine, according to Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps. The vessel was reportedly traveling on a route not agreed upon with Tehran. No casualties have been reported so far.

item.title: Tariff Hikes Prompt Uzbek Consumers to Save Electricity and Gas, Ministry Reports
item.description: Uzbekistan's average monthly electricity consumption per subscriber decreased from 212 kWh in 2023 to 184 kWh in 2025, a 13% drop. Natural gas consumption fell by 21%, from 431 to 342 cubic meters. The Ministry of Economy and Finance attributes this to consumers becoming more mindful of energy efficiency following tariff reforms.

item.title: Tajikistan to Construct 51.4 km Road Along Rogun Reservoir
item.description: Tajikgidroelektmontazh (TGEM) has signed a contract to build the Saidon-Labijar road along the left bank of the Rogun Reservoir. The project, funded by the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank (AIIB), aims to improve transport links between settlements in the reservoir zone. The three-year project will construct 51.4 km of road, including main and access routes.

item.title: Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev Holds Talks with Cambodian Prime Minister Hun Manet
item.description: Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev met with Cambodian Prime Minister Hun Manet during his official visit to Kazakhstan. The leaders held talks in a limited format, discussing bilateral relations and expressing optimism for enhanced cooperation. Tokayev highlighted the historical significance of the visit, noting it was the first by a Cambodian prime minister to Kazakhstan.

item.title: Afghanistan's Hunger Crisis Worsens: 16 Million Face Food Insecurity Ahead of Winter
item.description: Afghanistan faces a deepening humanitarian crisis as approximately 16 million people struggle with food insecurity before winter. Acute malnutrition among women and children is rising. Officials warn that without urgent action, a third of the population could face hunger this winter due to inflation, unemployment, climate change, and declining aid.

item.title: Russia-Afghanistan Trade Volume Doubles in Six Months, Says Envoy
item.description: Trade between Russia and Afghanistan has doubled in the first six months of this year, according to Zamir Kabulov, Russia’s special presidential representative for Afghanistan. He noted this significant increase occurred despite Afghanistan's circumstances and emphasized the need for gradual, sustainable trade growth.

item.title: IMF Projects Tajikistan's Economy to Grow by 7.3% in 2026
item.description: The International Monetary Fund forecasts Tajikistan's economy to grow by 7.3% in 2026, one of the highest rates in the Caucasus and Central Asia. Higher growth is projected for Kyrgyzstan and Uzbekistan. Regional economic prospects remain dependent on Middle East conflict consequences. The IMF noted that favorable commodity prices, remittances, and ongoing reforms contribute to regional economic stability.

item.title: Russia's Lavrov Warns of Militants Infiltrating Central Asia from Afghanistan
item.description: Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov stated that militants from international extremist groups are attempting to enter Central Asian countries from Afghanistan, using both legal and illegal channels. He noted particular activity in Afghan areas bordering Tajikistan, Turkmenistan, and Uzbekistan, with potential infiltration disguised as refugees or tourists. Russia's special services identify the 'Vilayat Khorasan' group as a primary threat.

item.title: Russian Missile Strikes Hit Kharkiv and Dnipro, Causing Casualties and Damage
item.description: Russian forces launched missile attacks on Kharkiv and Dnipro on the evening of October 16, resulting in fatalities and injuries. Residential buildings were damaged in Kharkiv, with local authorities reporting significant destruction. This marks the latest in a series of strikes on the city, which has seen multiple casualties in recent weeks.

item.title: Tajikistan Discusses Financial Support for Entrepreneurs at Business Forum
item.description: A panel session on banking and insurance solutions for businesses was held in Tajikistan as part of the "Tajikistan, Forward!" entrepreneurs' forum. Participants discussed access to financing, digital services development, payment infrastructure expansion, and insurance market opportunities. The event was initiated by the National Bank of Tajikistan.

item.title: US Limits Starlink Access for Ukraine, Raising Concerns Over Military Communications
item.description: The United States has temporarily restricted Ukraine's military access to Starlink satellite internet, a crucial system for drone and troop command. This move raises questions about potential communication disruptions for Kyiv and whether Europe can offer viable alternatives. The implications for Ukraine's defense capabilities are significant.

item.title: Mysterious Death of 62-Year-Old Man in Istaravshan, Wife Hospitalized
item.description: A 62-year-old man died under mysterious circumstances in Istaravshan, with his wife hospitalized. The incident occurred on the night of October 10 in Bobotagho village. The exact cause of death is unknown, and prosecutors are investigating. The man's body showed stab wounds.

item.title: Trump Lifts New Sanctions and Tariffs Against Russia
item.description: US President Donald Trump has canceled new sanctions and tariffs against Russia, which were scheduled to take effect this week. Reuters reported that Trump prevented the implementation of these measures by issuing an executive order. The White House stated the cancellation serves US national interests.

item.title: Russia-Afghanistan Trade Volume Doubles in First Half of 2026, Envoy Reports
item.description: Trade turnover between Russia and Afghanistan doubled in the first six months of 2026, according to Russian Presidential Special Representative Zamir Kabulov. He noted this significant growth indicates strengthening economic ties, despite modest overall figures, as Afghanistan recovers from decades of foreign military presence.

item.title: Over 2 Kilograms of Drugs Seized in Surxondaryo; Enough to Poison 8,124 People
item.description: Over two kilograms of narcotic drugs were found in a citizen's home in Surxondaryo. According to the Ministry of Internal Affairs, the seized amount is sufficient to poison 8,124 people. A criminal case has been initiated regarding the incident.

item.title: Islom Madaminov Appointed Deputy Governor of Fergana Region
item.description: Islom Madaminov has been appointed as the Deputy Governor of the Fergana Region. Prior to this appointment, he served as an advisor at the Embassy of Uzbekistan in Saudi Arabia. Further details are available via the provided link.

item.title: Tajik Parliament Approves Construction of Antimony Processing Plant for $35 Million
item.description: Tajik lawmakers have approved the construction of an antimony processing plant with an investment of $35 million. The facility is projected to process over 150,000 tons of ore annually. This development aims to enhance the country's industrial capacity in mineral processing.
